newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Hepworth sees modest results rise.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Hepworth sees modest results rise.

text.p: British heating and building materials group Hepworth Plc said on Thursday it expected results to rise modestly this year despite the strong pound and higher pensions costs.

"I would expect results to move up modestly despite all these issues and challenges...the underlying momentum is there and we're doing the right things to ensure that carries on. Thereafter the worst will be over," John Carter, chief executive said in a telephone interview.
Hepworth said earlier that this year would be challenging because the strong pound would impact the translation of overseas earnings and impair export margins.

"We have had 10 months at current parities between the franc, mark and sterling which is something like an 18 percent adverse movement," Carter said, noting that 25 percent of Hepworth products manufactured in Britain were exported.
Carter said Hepworth's programme to cut costs would continue in the early part of this year. The company said earlier that redundancy costs of 6.7 million stg had held back operating profits in 1996.

Carter said around 500 jobs had been shed from the group's 9,000-strong workforce although 200 jobs had been created with new heating and pipe joint ventures in China. He said he would not rule out the possibility of further job cuts.
Asked how talks were progressing on the possible sale of the Hepworth Refractories business, Carter said the company was speaking to several interested parties.

"They are continuing...We announced this in October. If they (the talks) weren't promising I think we'd have known about that by now. We're talking to a number of parties and you've got to interpret that positively," Carter said.

Carter said this year would focus on geographic expansion and product innovation, chiefly in boilers and pipes. The company recently bought a stake in a Czech firm and was looking at Hungary, Lithuania, Belarus, Russia and further expansion in China.
"We are very pleased with our early progress in China where we have two factories coming on stream and the prospects of one or two more," he said.
